newSounds: Most letters are already familiar, but watch the softeners: c before e/i is ch (caffè = kahf-FEH) and g before e/i is j (grazie = GRAH-tsyeh); ch is always k and gh is always a hard g. gn is ny in canyon, gl before i/e is ly in million, qu is kw, and z is ts (zz is dz, and initial z is voiced in zero and zona). A single s between vowels is voiced like z (cosa = KOH-zah).
rhythm: Italian is syllable-timed, very close to your native Telugu: every syllable gets roughly equal time and the vowels stay short and pure (a = ah, e = eh, i = ee, o = oh, u = oo). Do not reduce vowels to a schwa the way English does.
registerFirst: Start with Lei and third-person verbs: Come sta? Parla inglese? Ha? Tu forms (Come stai?, Hai?, Puoi?) are for friends, children and people who offer them first. Lei is written with a capital when it means 'you'.
trap: Double consonants are real and change the word: ottanta (80) has a held tt, while otanta is not a word. Hold the first consonant a beat longer, as in Telugu ట్ట or న్న. Also keep vowels pure - sette is SEHT-teh, never 'sett' with an English schwa. Regional accents shift vowel openness a little, but this standard pronunciation is understood everywhere from Sicily to Ticino.
